stories.title: Cyclone Akvan to make landfall between Nellore and Tuni in Andhra as very severe storm on November 20
stories.summary: Andhra fishermen, still awaiting compensation for Cyclone Arnab’s losses, are told to stay ashore till November 20

article_sentences: Cyclone Akvan, expected to form over the Bay of Bengal on Monday evening, is very likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni by noon on November 20 as a very severe cyclonic storm, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in its forecast on Monday (November 16, 2026).
Winds at landfall may reach 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph.
That leaves about 500 km of coast in play, that is, nearly half of Andhra Pradesh’s 1,053-km shoreline.
Machilipatnam sits roughly in the middle.
Weather experts are monitoring the system as it may change its course again.
Initial forecasts had indicated that the system may move towards north coastal Andhra Pradesh.
The latest IMD bulletin places its landfall in central and south coastal Andhra Pradesh.
Previously, very severe cyclonic storm Arnab made landfall near Narsapur, part of central Andhra Pradesh, and severe cyclonic storm Murasu near Ongole in south coastal Andhra Pradesh.
Krishna district, of which Machilipatnam is a part, has seen devastating cyclones in the past, including the infamous 1977 Diviseema cyclone.
However, the district was spared much of the damage during Arnab and Murasu.
Meanwhile, the depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal concentrated into a deep depression over the southeast and southwest Bay of Bengal in the early hours of Monday (November 16, 2026).

The system moved north-northwestwards at 6 kmph during the past six hours, and at 8.30 a.m., it lay centred about 630 km east-northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 690 km west of Sri Vijaya Puram in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, 700 km east-southeast of Chennai in Tamil Nadu, 800 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and 910 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh CM Naidu directs officials to take precautionary measures to tackle cyclone
stories.summary: Naidu directs officials to deploy NDRF and SDRF teams in advance and keep electricity department personnel ready to restore power supply on a war footing in the event of disruptions
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has on Monday directed officials to take precautionary measures in view of the cyclone expected to affect the Coastal Andhra region on November 20.
The Chief Minister reviewed the prevailing situation at the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) Centre in Amaravati today.
He instructed officials to continuously monitor the system and take all necessary precautionary measures.
Officials informed the Chief Minister that the severe depression currently centred over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify further and develop into a cyclone by this evening.
The Chief Minister directed the officials to consider the recommendations of Central assessment team and ensure their implementation at the field level.
The cyclone, developing over the Bay of Bengal, could bring moderate to heavy rainfall along the Coastal Andhra coast on November 19 and 20, according to officials.
It is likely to affect several areas, including Konaseema, Kakinada, East Godavari, West Godavari, Krishna, NTR and Guntur districts.

In view of the impending threat, the Chief Minister directed officials to deploy NDRF and SDRF teams in advance and keep electricity department personnel ready to restore power supply on a war footing in the event of disruptions.
He also instructed officials to take necessary steps to divert floodwaters resulting from heavy rainfall into reservoirs to ensure effective water management, according to a release.

stories.headline: BJP parts ways with Jana Sena, TDP in Bhimavaram Municipal election citing violation of alliance dharma
stories.title: BJP parts ways with Jana Sena, TDP in Bhimavaram Municipal election citing violation of alliance dharma
stories.summary: Union Minister and Narsapuram BJP MP Bhupathiraju Srinivas Varma announced that BJP would go alone in the Bhimavaram election, accusing the alliance partners of violating alliance dharma over seat-sharing.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The BJP has parted ways with its NDA alliance partners, the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and the Jana Sena Party (JSP), accusing them of violating alliance dharma after the latter filed nomination papers for all 47 ward councillors in the Bhimavaram Municipal election in West Godavari district allegedly without consulting the BJP on seat allocation.

Speaking to the media on Monday, Union Minister of State for Steel and Narsapuram BJP MP Bhupathiraju Srinivas Varma announced; “Our party has parted ways with our alliance partners - Jana Sena and TDP - as they filed nominations in all the 47 wards without any talks or consultation with our party in the Bhimavaram Municipal election.
We have decided to go our own way to prove our mettle in the election”.
The deadline to filing nominations for the councillors post ended on Monday.
Expressing resentment over the violation of the alliance dharma, the BJP filed nomination papers in nearly 30 wards.
“In the seat-sharing agreement, we were allotted five seats.
However, the JSP and TDP did not consult our party on the allocation of wards and proceeded with filing nominations, ignoring the BJP and the alliance dharma”, said Mr. Srinivas Varma.
He further alleged that the alliance partners had left three wards surrounding his residence for the BJP to contest without any talks or communication.
“We did not file nomination papers in those three wards as we do not want our party’s presence to be bound only to my area in the Bhimavaram municipality”, stated Mr. Srinivas Varma.
“The alliance partners even released and published the final candidates’ list for the 47 wards online without consultating with the BJP.
They ignored our party’s role in deciding and sharing the seats in the wards.
In the case of One Town Area in Bhimavaram, not a single seat of the 33 seats has been allotted to the BJP.

stories.title: Congress leaders stage protest outside Tripura State Election Commission office over civic polls

article_sentences: Senior Congress leaders staged a sit-in outside the State Election Commissioner’s office at the old Secretariat complex in Agartala on Monday (November 16, 2026), protesting alleged attempts to reduce the upcoming civic polls to a farce.
Tripura Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) president Ashish Kumar Saha, along with MLAs Sudip Roy Barman and Gopal Chandra Roy, joined the protest.
Congress alleged that the State Election Commission has remained completely silent despite large-scale irregularities, targeted attacks, and threats.
Mr. Saha said the police remained mere spectators and took no legal action against the perpetrators from the ruling BJP.
Elections to 21 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) comprising Nagar Panchayats and municipal bodies, including the Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC), will be held on November 27.
The BJP has already won five civic bodies unopposed as the Opposition and independent candidates refrained from filing nominations.
“As you are aware, the BJP won by using muscle power and government machinery in five councils.
They have created anarchy to capture the rest of the ULBs through unethical means and violence,” Mr. Saha told reporters.
State Election Commission officials failed to pacify the Congress leaders until senior police officers and the IGP arrived.
IGP Monchak Ippar briefed Congress leaders on security deployment and the measures to hold a free and fair election.
Meanwhile, the State Election Commission has requested 25 companies of Central Armed.
Police Forces (CAPF) for deployment during the elections through the State government.

stories.headline: ‘Unprecedented’ commodity costs squeeze auto industry margins in Q2
stories.title: ‘Unprecedented’ commodity costs squeeze auto industry margins in Q2
stories.summary: Top carmakers and two-wheeler companies reported strong volumes in the September quarter, with records at Maruti, Hyundai and TVS, helped by a demand boost from last September’s GST cut even as a steep rise in commodity costs squeezed margins.Maruti Suzuki, the country’s largest carmaker, and Hyundai Motor India reported profit falls of about 26 percent and 24 percent, respectively, even as revenue rose. Mahindra & Mahindra’s auto business, Bajaj Auto and TVS Motor posted strong profit growth on richer product mix and price increases, with exports also helping the two two-wheeler players.Tata Motors posted a loss, hit by restructuring costs at JLR.Input costs jumped for all manufacturers on the back of the West Asia conflict.Flagging the extent of the pressure, Mahindra’s group chief financial officer Amarjyoti Barua said copper prices are up 42 percent from a year ago, rubber is up 40 percent and steel is up 17 percent.Also Read: Car sales in October up 14-15 percent, cross 5 lakh for first time this fiscalPassenger VehiclesMaruti’s consolidated net profit fell to Rs 2,466 crore from Rs 3,349 crore a year earlier, even as revenue from operations rose 26 percent to Rs 53,356 crore. Its Ebitda margin narrowed to 9.4 percent from 12.7 percent. Other income fell to Rs 414 crore from Rs 946 crore, which the company attributed to mark-to-market losses on its invested surplus. Sales were a record 6,96,654 vehicles, up 26.5 percent.Hyundai’s profit fell 23.9 percent to Rs 1,196.2 crore on revenue that rose 18.5 per cent to Rs 20,696 crore, crossing Rs 20,000 crore for the first time. Its Ebitda margin narrowed to 9.5 percent from 13.9 percent.KS Hariharan, head of investor relations, put the raw material hit at about 400 basis points year-on-year. Total sales were a record 2,19,072 units, up 14.7 percent.Also Read: Car sales fall 14 percent in October as buyers defer purchases to NovemberTata Motors Passenger Vehicles posted a consolidated net loss of Rs 5,451 crore in the quarter as it booked a Rs 6,738 core loss in "exceptional items", which primarily included provision towards employee separation costs and impairment of assets at JLR.At Rs 96,920 crore, consolidated revenue was up 34 percent. Revenue from its domestic business, which excludes JLR, rose 50.9 percent to Rs 20,423 crore, its highest ever for a quarter.Ebitda margin was 6.2, up 630 basis points YoY while Ebit margin was 1.1 percent, up 790 bps YoY. The improvement mainly reflects recovery from the cyber incident at JLR last year, it said.Mahindra’s auto business bucked the trend. Its profit rose 55 percent to Rs 2,388 crore, helped by demand for its higher-priced SUVs, while consolidated revenue rose 39 percent to Rs 37,756 crore. Volumes rose 26 percent to about 3,31,000 units and its SUV revenue market share was 24.3 percent. Its profit margin before interest and tax was 8.8 percent, down from 9.3 percent a year ago but up from 7.7 percent in the June quarter. For the group as a whole, consolidated net profit rose 25 percent to Rs 4,588 crore.Margins improved from the June quarter at all three, except for Tata Motors. Maruti’s standalone Ebitda margin rose 80 basis points from 8.6 percent, and Hyundai’s rose to 9.5 percent from 9.3 percent. For Tata’s domestic business, Ebitda margin fell from 4.3 percent to 4 percent.Price HikesCarmakers have taken multiple rounds of price hikes this year but had held back during the festive season so as not to disrupt demand.Mahindra raised car prices by 5 percent and farm equipment prices by 4 percent to offset higher costs. Barua said further increases would be used only if the cost pressures looked structural.Maruti has raised prices three times and plans another round “at the appropriate timing” in the second half. Managing Director and CEO Hisashi Takeuchi said the company wants to keep demand momentum while pushing through the increases.Hyundai has also taken three increases this year, with the next scheduled for January. Managing Director and CEO Tarun Garg said the company had absorbed as much of the rise as it could in the hope that prices would come down, but that had not happened. “As of now, we will try to restrain,” he said on whether prices might rise before January.Tata has raised prices three times this year, most recently by up to Rs 25,000 from September 1. It plans to continue calibrated pricing actions.Also Read: India-made Mercedes for global markets? A matter of when, not if, says group CEOManaging the SqueezeMaruti has cut sales promotion and advertising spending by about 35 percent, according to Partho Banerjee, senior executive officer, marketing & sales. It is also hedging against commodity swings, working to improve material yields and has made some supply arrangements with vendors.Hyundai held discounts to 2.9 percent of sales from 3.2 percent a year earlier, and credited a better product mix and continuing cost cuts for the sequential improvement in profit.For Maruti and Mahindra, the constraint is supply rather than demand.Maruti has repeatedly flagged production constraints and even after adding capacity, it ended Q2 with a “low network inventory of about 17 days and pending bookings of about 200,000 units”.M&M’s Rajesh Jejurikar, who is executive director & CEO (auto and farm sector), said the company is operating at or above full capacity, and dealer stocks are down to eight or nine days in most of the portfolio.Group CEO Anish Shah said SUV capacity will rise from 64,500 a month at the start of the fiscal year to 82,000 by March and 1,32,000 by the end of fiscal 2031, when a new plant at Nagpur comes on stream.Tata Motors has also flagged production constraints in EVs, mainly because of insufficient capacity at suppliers.Rural stress and outlookThe monsoon this year has been the weakest in more than a decade, with a 13 percent rainfall deficit, and parts of the country face drought.The strain showed most clearly in Mahindra’s farm business. Consolidated farm revenue fell 6 per cent to Rs 9,572 crore and profit fell 9 percent to Rs 1,053 crore. Tractor volumes fell 6 percent to about 1,16,000 units. The company cut its forecast for the tractor industry to flat sales for the full year from 5 percent growth earlier.Jejurikar said the rainfall deficit is worse than expected, reservoir levels are low and farmers face higher input costs. Maharashtra and Karnataka have seen sharp falls in tractor demand, while Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and parts of Rajasthan are holding up.He said a clearer picture would emerge by late November, once festive buying ends.The festive season began later this year, on October 11, compared with September last year.Carmakers were more optimistic for now. Maruti Chairman RC Bhargava said rural demand has been growing slightly faster than urban, and that the future looks “quite rosy” despite a poor monsoon and an active El Nino. Hyundai said rural’s share of its sales hit a record 26.6 percent, though Garg said El Nino and the monsoon deficit were “worrying everybody”. “We are not seeing any slowdown as such,” he said, adding that it was “still early days”.Tata Motors sees volume growth of 12-13 percent this fiscal.Tata and Mahindra are vying for the position of India’s second-largest passenger vehicle maker after Maruti. Mahindra overtook Hyundai for the number two spot in calendar 2025, and Tata has held it for much of this year, helped by strong EV sales.Maruti’s Bhargava said the half-year was among its best ever. Hyundai kept its full-year Ebitda margin guidance of 11-14 percent, though Garg declined to give a timeline for recovery, saying industry consensus was that raw material prices should start easing after the US midterm elections. The company is targeting 8-10 percent growth in domestic sales this year.Mahindra kept its guidance of mid-to-high-teens SUV volume growth for the year and expects double-digit growth in light commercial vehicles. Shah said it would feel some pressure in the third quarter as commodity prices stay high, with an improvement in the fourth and a return to normal in the first quarter of next fiscal year.Also Read: Bajaj, TVS, Hero post strong Q2 profit; industry sales grow 27 percentTwo-wheelersThe three listed two-wheeler makers also posted strong revenue growth as domestic demand, an export surge and fast-rising e-scooter sales outweighed the cost increase, though profit growth varied sharply.Industry retail sales rose more than 27 percent in the quarter, with internal combustion engine (ICE) models up 23 percent and electric vehicles up 82 per cent.Bajaj Auto booked Rs 20,000 crore in revenue for the first time in a quarter. Revenue from operations rose 34 percent to Rs 20,003 crore and net profit rose 35 percent to Rs 3,354 crore. Ebitda climbed 37 percent to Rs 4,172 crore and the margin was 20.9 percent, up 40 basis points from a year earlier. Volumes rose 20 per cent to 15.49 lakh units.TVS Motor’s revenue rose 44 percent to Rs 17,103 crore, Ebitda rose 47 percent to Rs 2,219 crore and the margin widened 30 basis points to 13.0 percent. Net profit rose 52 percent to Rs 1,377 crore on a record 19.19 lakh units, up 27 per cent.Hero’s standalone revenue rose 21 percent to Rs 14,687 crore, but Ebitda rose only 8 percent to Rs 1,968 crore and net profit grew 5 percent to Rs 1,456 crore. Its Ebitda margin was 13.4 percent, up 10 basis points from the June quarter but down about 164 basis points from a year earlier. Wholesale volumes rose 10.5 percent to 18.68 lakh units, the weakest increase of the three. Consolidated profit rose 41 percent to Rs 1,861 crore, helped by a one-time Rs 397 crore gain from the equity dilution of an associate company.Bajaj said commodity and other input inflation was about 3-3.5 percent of revenue in the quarter, on top of about 4.5 percent in the first quarter, and called the scale of the escalation “unprecedented”. Price increases covered 50-60 percent of the impact in the first half, with the balance largely offset by favourable currency realisation and cost optimisation.TVS said material costs rose about 1.9 percent from the June quarter, against price increases of 1.6 percent. It has taken small increases in October and will review pricing after Diwali.Hero said commodity inflation was about 1 percent sequentially and that about half of the roughly 5.5 percent cumulative inflation in the first half has been passed on. It said margins should be stable in the third quarter and that it remains on track toward its 14-16 percent medium-term target.Exports helped Bajaj and TVS offset costs through a better mix and favourable currency movement. Bajaj’s exports rose 41 percent, TVS’s 35 percent while Hero’s overseas dispatches fell about 24 percent, hurt by port and customs disruption after an earthquake in a key Latin American market and weaker demand in Bangladesh.Entry-level StressHero’s weaker showing points to stress at the bottom of the pyramid. Around 85 per cent of its domestic volume comes from entry-level motorcycles (75cc to 110cc).Bajaj’s management said growth is skewed toward higher-income buyers, with entry-level products lagging, a “K-shaped” pattern that may get sharper. Bajaj raised prices on 100cc models ahead of rivals and accepted weaker volumes there.Hero said rural performance matched or beat urban in the quarter and so far in the festive period, and said fears of a weak monsoon have not fully played out, with sowing close to last year’s level.Jay Kale, director-institutional equity research at Elara Capital, said EVs were another reason behind Hero’s numbers. “Hero’s EV business is just ramping up, so commodity pressures in terms of EV losses are higher for them compared to the others.”Also Read: How India's Alternative Fuel Car Boom Is Spreading Beyond Top StatesEV PlayListed pure-play EV player Ather Energy reported its first ever net profit in Q2, becoming the first major standalone company in the country to turn a profit.Electric vehicles were also the fastest-growing segment at all the three legacy players. Bajaj's electric two- and three-wheelers reached a record 2 lakh units, now a third of its domestic revenue, and its Chetak scooter had revenue above Rs 2,000 crore and a market share of about 23 percent. TVS sold 1.86 lakh electric two-wheelers, up 133 percent. Hero's EV market share was 11.1 per cent in the quarter.Managements expect growth to slow from the H1 pace.Hero’s CEO Harshavardhan Chitale expects the industry to grow at mid-to-high single digits in the festive period and the second half, with ICE models growing at low single digits and EVs lifting the overall number.TVS Managing Director K N Radhakrishnan expects “good single-digit” growth in the third quarter, while Bajaj Joint Managing Director Rakesh Sharma expects the December growth to stay in double digits but below the April-August rate, and warned that drought-like conditions in Maharashtra, parts of the south and the northeast could hurt more in the fourth quarter.

Managements expect growth to slow from the H1 pace.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court warned of initiating contempt action if the Union government and authorities did not give a detailed and thorough response to an application filed by advocate Amar Jain pointing out that many visually-impaired and low-vision persons are still unable to independently complete their Aadhaar face authentication.

A Bench headed by Justice JB Pardiwala issued notice on Jain’s application pointing out that the inability to complete Aadhaar face authentication was affecting e-KYC, which only relies on face authentication.
“The new Aadhaar App with face authentication interface which persons with blindness are unable to complete as it requires eyes to be attentive and looking into the frame,” the application said.
Jain said he had personally suffered the obstacles pointed out by him in his application before the court.

“There is no grievance mechanism for accessibility complaints against apps, websites and software… Accessibility audits, nodal officers, human review of rejected KYC applications and compliance monitoring are not visible across regulated entities,” the application noted.
He has annexed with his application what he said was the “latest rejection by a private sector bank of my e-KYC for a credit card in October 2026”.

Jain, represented by advocate-on-record Ila Sheel, said the continued lack of easy access was in violation of a Supreme Court judgment of 2025 in Pragya Prasun versus Union of India that had given comprehensive directions to ease digital access for the disabled.

“Amidst this wave of digital progress, there remains a crucial and often overlooked aspect that demands urgent attention – ensuring that digital infrastructure and services are accessible to all, including persons with disabilities and other marginalised groups.
True inclusion requires that technological advancements accommodate the diverse needs of all citizens,” the court had observed in the 2025 judgment.
Jain was one of the parties in the Pragya Prasun case.

He urged the apex court to intervene, once again, to direct the Union government, the Reserve Bank of India, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Telecom Regulatory Authority of India, Department of Telecommunications, Securities and Exchange Board of India, Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority, and Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India to fully implement the 2025 judgment.

The application has sought a clarification from the Ministry on how it intended to handle accessibility complaints about unregulated digital platforms and provide a mechanism to monitor compliance by regulated entities.

article_sentences: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has moved the Supreme Court seeking a review of its 15 October judgment that struck down Yes Bank’s ₹8,415-crore write-down of additional tier-1 (AT-1) bonds.
According to the Supreme Court website, the RBI filed its review petition on 13 November.
The central bank is seeking reconsideration of the judgment, which upheld an earlier Bombay High Court ruling quashing the write-down.
Yes Bank had also filed a review petition on 13 November, making it the second party to seek a review of the Supreme Court’s judgment.
A review petition is not a fresh appeal.
Under Article 137 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court can review its own judgments on limited grounds, such as an error apparent on the face of the record or other sufficient reason.
The court normally hears such petitions through its review jurisdiction, and only in exceptional cases does it reopen a matter.
A review petition is generally heard in chambers by the same bench that passed the original judgment.
The dispute goes back to Yes Bank’s rescue in March 2020, when the bank was facing severe financial stress.
The Centre imposed a moratorium on the lender on 5 March, and the RBI superseded its board and appointed an administrator.
A draft reconstruction scheme initially proposed permanently writing down Yes Bank’s AT-1 bonds.
However, the provision was removed from the final scheme notified by the government on 13 March 2020.

stories.headline: Rural economy: Resilient but uneven; next few quarters key
stories.title: Rural economy: Resilient but uneven; next few quarters key
stories.summary: The 2026 southwest monsoon ended on September 30 at 87 percent of the long period average (LPA), a deficit of nearly 13 percent. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) recorded it as the driest season since 2015. A strong El Niño, drought conditions in several states, reservoirs well below last year's levels and retail inflation above 6 percent in October have clouded the outlook for the farm economy.East and northeast India had their driest monsoon on record. By September 11, the area sown with kharif crops stood at 109.65 million hectares, against 111.25 million hectares a year earlier. Paddy accounted for much of the decline. The Central Water Commission's bulletin of October 15 showed the 178 reservoirs it monitors at 68.58 percent of capacity. That was 24.53 percent lower than a year earlier, and 16.44 percent below the 10-year average.Also Read: Rural young women face rising joblessness“The state of rural economy will largely be guided by the performance of the kharif crop,” said Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at Bank of Baroda. “This will determine the overall demand conditions from this side.”On September 29, the agriculture ministry set a foodgrain production target of 373.93 million tonnes for 2026-27, below the record 376.56 million tonnes of 2025-26. Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said he did not expect a significant fall in kharif output. The ministry has not yet released its first advance estimates for the 2026-27 kharif crop.Sabnavis says El Niño has already shown up in rainfall, but its effect on crops will be clear only when the ministry releases its advance estimates. “The reservoir levels are much lower than last year which poses a challenge for animal husbandry and rabi crop,” he said. “Given the drought conditions in various regions like Maharashtra, Karnataka, AP and Telangana, we could expect a pushback.”Lekha Chakraborty, a professor at NIPFP in New Delhi, says past El Niño episodes typically reduced kharif yields, real wages and discretionary spending. “Their effects on employment schemes and farm equipment sales can be seen later. The 2023–24 episode turned out milder than feared because of better irrigation and buffer stocks,” she said, adding, “Key challenges ahead include reservoir stress in critical regions, input-cost volatility, and the possibility that food-price spikes erode real incomes even if overall agricultural GVA holds up better than in earlier decades,” she says.Also Read: Bringing rural entrepreneurs online through assisted e-commerceThe Food billThe higher food prices are now reaching consumers as well. Amul and Mother Dairy raised milk prices by Rs 2 per litre in May. Mother Dairy announced a second increase of Rs 2– 4 per litre from November 12, citing procurement, cattle feed and transport costs. Maize makes up 55–65 percent of cattle feed, and dairy companies say a growing share of it is being diverted to ethanol production.Sabnavis points to both supply and diversion. “Sugar price going up could partly be due to lower output as well as diversion of cane for ethanol,” he says. “In the case of milk, the cost of feed has gone up which pushes up the price of milk. With maize prices being erratic due to lower expected output and oilcake prices rising, it has fed into the price of milk and other products like eggs, meat etc.”Chakraborty says sugar price spikes have come mainly from production shortfalls against earlier estimates and thin carry-over stocks. Festive demand, crop damage, tighter global supply and occasional hoarding or delayed crushing have added to the pressure. Milk and other perishables face similar mismatches between supply and demand, which weather and logistics make worse. “Government interventions—stock limits, imports, and early crushing—mitigate volatility but do not eliminate it,” she said.Also Read: October retail inflation climbs to 6.09%, breaching RBI’s tolerance ceilingJobs schemes and subsidiesThe monsoon shortfall is also the first test of VB-G RAM G (Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin). The scheme replaced MGNREGA on July 1, 2026, and raised the guaranteed work from 100 to 125 days per household per year. Government data released in late October shows more than 31.69 crore person-days generated in 2026-27. Work went to about 2.23 crore rural households, and women made up 61.65 percent of participation.Chakraborty says the scheme's rollout has gone better than expected. “Early implementation appears smoother than feared, with higher women's participation and direct benefit transfers,” she says. She adds that lasting productivity gains from the expanded guarantee and its asset focus will depend on the quality of works and on local planning.Fertilisers and subsidies have also been an important part of the rural economy. The Union Cabinet on November 10 raised the per-kg subsidy rates under the nutrient-based subsidy regime for the rabi 2026-27 season. The revised rates have an outlay of Rs 62,370 crore, with sulphur seeing the highest increase. Earlier, a subsidy of Rs 41,534 crore was also announced for kharif 2026-27. The increase comes on the back of global non-urea fertiliser prices staying elevated. “Farm subsidies are necessary in these challenging times, and we need to have a long-term policy for making agri resilient,” said Sabnavis.Chakraborty calls for careful recalibration. She says input subsidies and open-ended procurement distort cropping patterns, encourage overuse of fertiliser and water, and carry large financial costs with uneven benefits. She suggests better targeting through digital platforms and a gradual move toward direct income support. She also suggests redirecting money to productivity, climate-resilient seed varieties and market infrastructure.Abhishek Mathur, lead analyst for consumer staples and paints at Systematix, notes that measures such as minimum support price (MSP) increases and rural employment benefits are already in place.Also Read: Can the Indian economy grow fast even as prices rise?RBI outlookOn October 7, the RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 percent. It was the first rate increase since February 2023, and the committee moved its stance from neutral to “calibrated tightening”. The MPC said the deficient monsoon and strong El Niño conditions posed risks to the farm outlook and rural demand. It added that healthy foodgrain buffers and government action were expected to soften the impact.The RBI raised its GDP growth forecast for 2026-27 to 7.1 percent, with quarterly estimates of 7.2 percent for Q2, 6.9 percent for Q3 and 6.8 percent for Q4. It put CPI inflation for the year at 5.2 percent, peaking at 6 percent in the October–December quarter. The committee said food price increases had become more widespread, with sharp rises in items such as sugar and onion. Governor Sanjay Malhotra noted that kharif sowing was somewhat above normal but marginally below last year.Inflation in October went past the RBI’s 6 percent upper limit. Provisional data for the month put CPI inflation at 6.09 percent, up from 5.54 percent in September. Inflation was higher in rural areas, at 6.63 percent, than in urban areas, at 5.41 percent. Rural food inflation rose to 9.09 percent from 8.06 percent.Chakraborty says the RBI's view of a rural economy less exposed to rainfall holds up. “The RBI assessment is largely accurate,” she says. “For small landholders, wages already contribute more than 55 percent of household income, while livestock and non-farm activities cushion crop shortfalls.” She also said that non-agricultural rural growth has stayed near 6 percent across different rainfall patterns. The statistical link between rainfall deficits and wider rural activity has weakened since the mid-2000s.What the September quarter numbers showHindustan Unilever (HUL), the country's largest FMCG company, reported underlying volume growth of 7 percent for Q2FY27. Underlying sales growth was 15 percent, its highest in 14 quarters. Management said rural markets had improved quarter after quarter while urban growth stayed steady. CEO Priya Nair said structural factors were supporting the farm economy despite below-normal rains.Dabur India grew consolidated revenue 11.6 percent to Rs 3,563 crore. Its India FMCG business grew 10.7 percent, with volume growth of 5.5 percent. Godrej Consumer Products said uneven rains and inflation had hurt consumption, but it still expected high single-digit underlying volume growth.“As noted by Dabur (sales more exposed to rural markets), the growth in rural demand is currently higher against growth in urban by 150bps,” said Mathur. “So at present, rural consumption seems to be holding strong. However, this remains monitorable over the next 3-4 quarters when the impact of a deficient monsoon becomes clearer.”Data from the market tracker NielsenIQ (NIQ) for the June quarter showed rural FMCG volumes down 5 percent year on year, with 68 percent of categories shrinking. Urban volumes were broadly flat, at 0.1 percent. Traditional trade, which carries about 82 percent of FMCG sales nationally, lost 6 percent in volume. Modern trade grew 17.5 percent and e-commerce 34.8 percent.Sabnavis says urban India's FMCG outlook looks good despite inflation, but rural India is still uncertain. “For rural India, it needs to be seen how it works,” he said. He adds that firms have been changing their packaging to reach rural buyers.Why rural demand is hard to measureAmid a number of macro indicators, economists remain divided over one question: How to measure rural demand. After the April–June quarter, HUL's management cited continued growth in two-wheeler and tractor sales as signs of rural demand.Sabnavis says it is hard to figure out the true level of rural consumption and statements made by FMCG or auto sales. “Tractors are never purchased every year and hence can be misleading. Even for two-wheelers, using this as a proxy can be misleading as urban India has also seen a boom post Covid,” he said.Mathur says a smaller farm sector cushions rural consumption. “As noted by HUL, the agri sector now contributes just 15 percent to GDP, and has been coming down over the past several years. Also, 30-35 percent of income for the rural population comes from non-agri sources,” he said. “So yes, these seem to be likely reducing the impact of a deficient monsoon on rural consumption.”Also Read: VB-G RAM G's Debut Shows a Sharp Drop. Is It Cause for Concern?Chakraborty describes rural demand as “resilient yet uneven”. She cites NABARD's rural economic conditions and sentiments surveys (RECSS), which through late 2025 showed nearly 80 percent of households reporting higher consumption. The share of income spent on consumption rose to about 67 percent, helped by GST cuts and softer food inflation.“Aggregate data captures only part of the story: Households with diversified non-farm incomes fare better, while those dependent on rain-fed crops remain vulnerable," she says. "Informal buffers, welfare transfers, and asset sales prop up reported spending while masking weaker farm returns."She suggests a wider set of indicators: Real rural wage trends and the split of household income between crops, wages and livestock. Savings and debt, and the inflation-adjusted split between food and non-food spending, also belong in the mix. High-frequency sentiment surveys and district-level data on non-farm activity should support these. “Metrics need to give more weight to income diversification and climate resilience, since pure agricultural output no longer fully tracks rural purchasing power,” she adds.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Clears Lulu Mall's Resolution Plan For Manjeera Retail Holdings
stories.title: Supreme Court Clears Lulu Mall's Resolution Plan For Manjeera Retail Holdings
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 16) has paved the way for the implementation of the resolution plan submitted by Lulu International Shopping Malls Private Limited for Manjeera Retail Holdings Private Limited, by dismissing as time-barred appeals challenging its approval.

A bench of Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva held that the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) could not have entertained the appeals filed beyond the maximum 45-day period prescribed under Section 61(2) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC).
Lulu International had emerged as the successful resolution applicant after its plan received 100% approval from the Committee of Creditors.
The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Hyderabad, approved the resolution plan on March 26, 2025.
Lulu International stated that it had invested ₹271.52 crore towards its implementation.

Three individuals who had entered into agreements to purchase commercial units in Manjeera Mall, Hyderabad challenged the approval, alleging that their payments towards the full sale consideration had been wrongly classified as “advances from customers” instead of recognising them as claims of financial creditors.
Under Section 61(2) of the IBC, an appeal against an NCLT order must be filed within 30 days, with a maximum additional 15 days available for condonation of delay.
In this case, the extended 45-day period expired on May 10, 2025, a second Saturday.
The respondents filed their appeals on May 11, 2025.

The NCLAT condoned the delay by applying Section 4 of the Limitation Act, 1963, which permits filing on the next working day when the court is closed on the last day of the prescribed limitation period.
Setting aside this order, the judgment authored by Justice Sanjay Kumar relied on its decision in Tata Steel Ltd.
Raj Kumar Banerjee 2025 LiveLaw (SC) 542, which clarified that Section 4 of the Limitation Act cannot extend the additional period available for condonation of delay under a special statute.

stories.headline: Supreme Court calls for encroachment-free Yamuna floodplain, penalties on states over pollution
stories.title: Supreme Court calls for encroachment-free Yamuna floodplain, penalties on states over pollution
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Observing that pollution in the Yamuna has only increased despite huge sums being spent on cleaning it, the Supreme Court has called for removal of encroachments from Zone ‘O’ floodplain area, surprise inspections of sewage treatment plants (STPs) and penalties on states and Union Territories where the river’s water quality deteriorates.

In its November 4 order, a bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Manmohan said that states and UTs through which the Yamuna flows must treat it as a shared resource rather than limit their responsibility to their respective stretches.
It sought a formula for imposing penalties to end the practice of “passing the buck”.

“Everything that is wrong with civic administration in the towns, cities and villages situated along the banks of the river is reflected in the poor health of the river and in the 520 drains” that discharge wastewater into it, the bench observed.
“This is why, despite huge sums being spent on cleaning the river, pollution in the Yamuna has only increased,” it added.

The court was examining a Yamuna Action Plan prepared by a committee headed by the Union Home Secretary, which it called is “a significant step forward… as it identifies domestic sewage as the single largest source of pollution entering Yamuna”.
The plan proposes 125 new STPs, 12 common effluent treatment plants (CETPs), 10 municipal solid waste plants and 23 biogas plants, besides upgrading existing facilities.

However, the bench noted that while the plan stated that water bodies and wetlands along Zone ‘O’ – Yamuna’s designated riverfront zone in the Capital – were free of encroachments, an annexure to the draft Yamuna Action Plan, prepared by the Delhi government, marked all 35 such water bodies and wetlands in the area as encroached upon.

“Further, although the Plan states that 28 of the 38 existing STPs in Delhi meet the standards… the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) in its report… states that none of these plants meets all the prescribed standards and that only five meet the bacteriological limit,” it added.

The bench said, “…unless illegal and unauthorised colonies, JJ clusters on the drains as well as on the riverbed are removed after rehabilitating their occupants, their sewage will continue to pollute the river at the source.”
The bench said Zone ‘O’, as defined in Delhi Master Plan-2047, should be protected as a green zone and, if feasible, extended from the Yamuna’s source to its confluence with the Ganga.
It added that no permanent structures should be permitted in this zone in future, except green parks and essential public infrastructure.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Awards Rs. 30 Lakhs To Man Kept In Jail For 7 Years Despite Acquittal, Recommends Law To Compensate Illegal Custody
stories.title: Supreme Court Awards Rs. 30 Lakhs To Man Kept In Jail For 7 Years Despite Acquittal, Recommends Law To Compensate Illegal Custody
stories.summary: The Court noted that the Chhattisgarh authorities displayed "complete remissness" in the matter.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Court noted that the Chhattisgarh authorities displayed "complete remissness" in the matter.

The Supreme Court on Monday (November 16) awarded compensation of ₹30 lakh to a man who remained in prison for over seven years despite being acquitted due to a gap in communication of his acquittal order with the jail authorities.

Describing the prolonged incarceration as a failure of the criminal justice administration to secure his release, the Court also highlighted the absence of a statutory framework in India to compensate individuals for wrongful incarceration and underscored the need for a legislative mechanism to address such cases.

The Court also directed all the High Courts to consider issuing directions similar to those issued by the Madhya Pradesh High Court and to consider establishing an Online Criminal Justice Ecosystem to ensure timely communication and implementation of judicial orders.
“The High Court of Madhya Pradesh has also launched an Online Criminal Justice Ecosystem.
The Online Criminal Justice Ecosystem is an integrated platform for Police, Courts, Prisons, Prosecution, Forensics & Hospitals.
It facilitates sharing of online criminal justice data among all stakeholders.
These systems help in improving efficiency and transparency and provide speedy justice to citizens.
It digitises and streamlines the bail processing workflow and all related activities under criminal justice system.
The Online Criminal Justice Ecosystem has been launched to inter alia ensure immediate sharing of information between the various stake holder.

Be it the Police, Courts, Prisons, Prosecution, Forensics or Hospitals, it facilitates transmission of data, case diaries, medical & forensic reports and court orders in a prompt and secure atmosphere ensuring timely service and compliances.”, the Court said.
The court ordered circulation of a copy of this judgment to the Registrar Generals of all the High Courts for placing the same before the respective Chief Justices for their consideration.
